Munich massacre: 1972 Summer Olympics terrorist attack. The militants infiltrated the Olympic Village, killed two members of the Israeli Olympic team, and took nine other Israeli team members hostage.
Emerging in the 1970s among disillusioned liberal hawks, this political movement peaked in influence under George W. Bush and helped drive the push to invade Iraq in 2003 — what is it called?
Neoconservatism: Political movement of former liberals that combines political and social conservatism.
A Peronist who governed Argentina from 2003 to 2007, he later became the country's first 'first gentleman' when his wife succeeded him as president — who was he?

Néstor Kirchner: President of Argentina from 2003 to 2007. Néstor Carlos Kirchner Ostoić (25 February 1950 – 27 October 2010) was an Argentine lawyer and politician who served as the president of Argentina from 2003 to 2007.

One of the Three Kingdoms of Korea alongside Goguryeo and Silla, this kingdom in the southwest had the largest population of the three and was founded by Onjo near present-day Seoul. Which kingdom was it?
Paekche: Ancient Korean kingdom (18 BCE – 660 CE)
Considered the most influential artist of the Flemish Baroque, this painter and diplomat was known for dramatic, sensual compositions and designs for tapestry workshops — who is he?
Peter Paul Rubens: Flemish artist and diplomat (1577–1640)

Held every June in many cities to commemorate the 1969 Stonewall riots, this annual LGBTQ celebration of rights and self-acceptance began as marches in Chicago, New York, LA, and San Francisco in 1970 — what's it called?
Pride parade: LGBTQ celebration event. The events sometimes also serve as demonstrations for legal rights such as same-sex marriage.
This founding pharaoh of Egypt's 19th Dynasty had a brief reign that bridged the stable rule of his predecessor and the illustrious dynasty led by his son and grandson — who is he?
Ramesses I: Founding pharaoh of 19th dynasty of Egypt. The dates for his short reign are not completely known but the timeline of late 1292–1290 BC is frequently cited as well as 1295–1294 BC.

Born in Southampton to parents of Indian descent who fled East Africa, this British politician served as Chancellor of the Exchequer before rising to the nation's highest office in 2022—but his tenure lasted just two years before losing to Keir Starmer. Who is he?
Rishi Sunak: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 2022 to 2024.
Beginning on 24 February 2022, this conflict became the largest and deadliest war in Europe since World War II and sparked the continent's biggest refugee crisis in that span — what is it?
Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present): Phase since 2022 of war ongoing since 2014.
Leader of Spain's far-right Vox party since 2014 and president of Patriots.eu since 2024, this politician represents Madrid in the Congress of Deputies — who is he?
Named after the TV show in which its founder played a fictional president, this Ukrainian political party has ruled since Volodymyr Zelenskyy won the presidency in 2019 — which party?
Servant of the People: Political party in Ukraine. It was formed in late 2017 and was officially registered on 31 March 2018 on the basis of the previously registered Party of Decisive Changes.
Ruling from 893 to 927, this monarch's campaigns against the Byzantines and Magyars brought the First Bulgarian Empire to its greatest size and a cultural Golden Age — who was he?
Simeon I of Bulgaria: First Emperor of the Bulgars from 893 to 927.
A Princeton grad and former F-15 flight test engineer, he co-founded the deep-sea firm OceanGate and died in 2023 when its submersible imploded en route to the Titanic wreck — who was he?

As senior counselor to a Tokugawa shōgun, this Edo-period official pursued reforms that debased the currency and sold monopoly rights to merchants — remembered for both economic innovation and rampant corruption — who was he?
Tanuma Okitsugu: Japanese political advisor, rōjū (1719–1788)
Around the year 1010, this Icelandic explorer followed Leif Eriksson's route to Vinland with his wife Gudrid in a short-lived bid to found a permanent settlement — who was he?
This Indian revolutionary assassinated the former Punjab lieutenant governor in 1940 in revenge for the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre, of which he was a survivor — who was he?
Udham Singh: Indian revolutionary (1899–1940). Singh was subsequently tried and convicted of murder and hanged in July 1940.
In 1976, this Soviet pilot defected to the West by flying his MiG-25 'Foxbat' jet interceptor to Japan, handing the CIA what George H. W. Bush called an 'intelligence bonanza' — who is he?
Viktor Belenko: Soviet pilot who defected to the West (1947–2023)

Beginning with the 1916 death of Yuan Shikai, this chaotic decade-plus in Chinese history saw the country splinter under rival military cliques until Sun Yat-sen's Nationalists challenged the Beijing government for legitimacy — which period?
Warlord Era: Period in the history of the Republic of China (1916–1928)

Convinced that Protestants and the Catholic majority had to make common cause against the Crown, this revolutionary helped found the Society of United Irishmen in 1791 and became an icon of Irish republicanism — who was he?
A career Army general who became a national hero in the Mexican-American War, this 12th U.S. president died of a stomach illness just 16 months into office — who is he?
Zachary Taylor: President of the United States from 1849 to 1850.
Who among these was born first?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?

Oliver Heaviside (born 1850) is the earliest of the four. Although at odds with the scientific establishment for most of his life, Heaviside changed the face of telecommunications, mathematics, and science.
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four came first?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Bruno Rossi is an astronomer. Bruno Benedetto Rossi ( ROSS-ee, Italian: [ˈbruːno beneˈdetto ˈrossi]; 13 April 1905 – 21 November 1993) was an Italian-American experimental physicist.
Which of these four is a mathematician?
Hilary Putnam is a mathematician. Outside philosophy, Putnam contributed to mathematics and computer science.
What is the atomic number of Indium?
Indium: It is a silvery-white post-transition metal and one of the softest elements.
What is the atomic number of Scandium?
Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
In what year was Stephen Hawking born?
Stephen Hawking: Hawking was born in Oxford into a family of physicians.
In what year was Richard Sackler born?
Richard Sackler: Sackler and Purdue's role in the epidemic led to many lawsuits and fines, with the company filing bankruptcy in 2019.
In what year was Aristotle born?
Aristotle (Ancient Greek: Ἀριστοτέλης, romanized: Aristotélēs; 384–322 BC) was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath.
In what year did Abraham Maslow die?
Abraham Maslow: Maslow was a psychology professor at Cornell University, Brooklyn College, Brandeis University, The New School for Social Research, and Columbia University.
In what year did Kevin Mitnick die?
Kevin Mitnick: Kevin David Mitnick (August 6, 1963 – July 16, 2023) was an American computer security consultant, author, and convicted hacker.
In what year was Mass–energy equivalence discovered?
Mass–energy equivalence: In physics, mass–energy equivalence is the relationship between mass and energy in a system's rest frame.
Which company manufactures Harrier jump jet?
Harrier jump jet: Hawker Siddeley. The Harrier emerged as the only truly successful V/STOL design of the many attempted during that era.
NHIndustries NH90: Airbus Helicopters. The NHIndustries NH90 is a medium-sized European twin-engine multi-role military helicopter.
Which country is Hawker Hunter from?
Hawker Hunter: United Kingdom. The all-weather/night fighter role was filled by the Gloster Javelin.
Who is credited with discovering Bohrium?
Bohrium: Yuri Oganessian. Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
Who is credited with discovering 10 Hygiea?
10 Hygiea: Annibale de Gasparis. 10 Hygiea is a large asteroid in the outer region of the main asteroid belt, between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Who is credited with discovering Nickel?
Nickel: Axel Fredrik Cronstedt. Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
Home to both edible and poisonous species, this fungal genus supplies the West's most popular cultivated mushrooms, including the everyday button mushroom — which genus is it?
Agaricus is a genus of mushroom-forming fungi containing both edible and poisonous species, with over 400 members worldwide and possibly again as many disputed or newly discovered species.

This central nervous system stimulant treats ADHD and narcolepsy today, but was once prescribed for nasal congestion and depression, and remains tightly controlled due to its abuse potential — name the drug?

Amphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy; it is also used to treat binge eating disorder in the form of lisdexamfetamine.
Marked by right lower abdominal pain, nausea, and fever, this common inflammatory condition is typically caused by a blockage from a small hard mass called a fecalith — name the condition?
Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
This 2023 Telugu period action thriller stars Ravi Teja in the title role but became a box-office bomb despite its ambitions. What film is it?
Badger are medium-sized short-legged omnivores in the superfamily Musteloidea.
First coined in 1919 by Hungarian engineer Károly Ereky, this multidisciplinary field harnesses living organisms like bacteria and yeast to make products and services. What field is it?

Biotechnology is a multidisciplinary field that involves the integration of natural sciences and engineering sciences to achieve the application of organisms and parts thereof for products and services.
Named in a 2018 New York Times essay by Bari Weiss as part of the 'intellectual dark web,' this former evolutionary biology professor left academia after 2017 campus protests — who is he?
Bret Weinstein (born February 21, 1969) is an American podcaster, author, and former professor of evolutionary biology.
First classified by Linnaeus in 1753, which herbaceous annual takes its specific name from the Latin for 'cultivated' and has long supplied fiber, seed oil, food and medicine?
Cannabis sativa is an annual herbaceous flowering plant.

The scientific study of matter's properties and behavior, this physical science occupies an intermediate position between physics and biology, sometimes called the central science. What is this field of study?
Chemistry is the scientific study of the properties and behavior of matter. Chemistry also addresses the nature of chemical bonds in chemical compounds.
Once a standard topical anesthetic prized for narrowing blood vessels, this tropane alkaloid is extracted from the leaves of South American coca plants — which substance is it?
Cocaine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and tropane alkaloid, derived primarily from the leaves of two coca species native to South America.
Native to North America and smaller than its close relative the gray wolf, this canine fills a similar ecological niche to the golden jackal of Eurasia — which animal?
Coyote (Canis latrans) is a species of canine also known as the American jackal, prairie wolf, and brush wolf.

This common cough suppressant found in cold medicine was combined with bupropion in 2022 to create a fast-acting antidepressant, despite belonging to the same chemical class as morphine — what drug is it?
Dextromethorphan is a cough suppressant used in many cough and cold medicines.
Along with the platypus, this quill-covered Australian and New Guinean mammal is one of only two living egg-laying mammal groups, and its young are adorably called puggles — what is it?
Echidna are quill-covered monotremes (egg-laying mammals) belonging to the family Tachyglossidae, living in Australia and New Guinea.
This Ancient Greek polymath, who became chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria, is considered the founder of geography as a discipline and coined much of its early terminology — who is he?

Patented in 1979 but not used medically until 1996, this second-generation antihistamine treats allergic rhinitis and hives while causing far less drowsiness than older allergy medications — what's the drug?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine medication used in the treatment of allergy symptoms such as allergic rhinitis and urticaria.
Reclassified twice before settling into its own genus, this Gram-variable, non-spore-forming coccobacillus is barely one to 1.5 micrometers across — which species?
Gardnerella vaginalis is a species of Gram-variable-staining facultative anaerobic bacteria.

This American computer scientist and Navy rear admiral devised the theory of machine-independent programming languages and used it to help create COBOL, after being one of the first programmers on the Harvard Mark I — who is she?
Grace Hopper (ne Murray; December 9, 1906 - January 1, 1992) was an American computer scientist, mathematician, and United States Navy rear admiral.

His synergy with information-theory father Claude Shannon laid foundations for the Information Age, and during WWII he helped build automatic guns that defended London from V-1 flying bombs — who was this Dutch-American control-theory pioneer?
Hendrik Wade Bode (-d,; December 24, 1905 - June 21, 1982) was an American engineer, researcher, inventor, author and scientist, of Dutch ancestry.
This thin piece of mucosal tissue that surrounds or partially covers the vaginal opening takes its name from a Greek word meaning 'thin skin' — name the structure?
Hymen is a thin piece of mucosal tissue that surrounds or partially covers the vaginal opening. It forms part of the vulva and is similar in structure to the vagina.
One of the largest dog breeds in the world, this sighthound was historically used to course game and became the official mascot of a British Guards regiment in 1902. What breed is it?
Irish Wolfhound is a breed of large sighthound that has, by its presence and substantial size, inspired literature, poetry and mythology.
Two years after unveiling the first mechanical television system, this Scottish engineer achieved the first-ever transatlantic television transmission in 1928 — who is he?
John Logie Baird (13 August 1888 - 14 June 1946) was a Scottish inventor, electrical engineer and innovator who demonstrated the world's first mechanical television system on 26 January 1926.
Named after a 19th-century Russian neuropsychiatrist, which memory disorder features confabulation and amnesia from vitamin B1 deficiency, often following an episode of Wernicke encephalopathy?
Korsakoff syndrome (KS) is a disorder of the central nervous system characterized by amnesia, deficits in explicit memory, and confabulation.
Also called the great grey slug, this 10-20cm mollusc has a strange courtship where mating pairs suspend themselves in midair from a mucus thread — what species is it?
Limax maximus (literally, "biggest slug"), known by the common names great grey slug and leopard slug, is a species of slug in the family Limacidae, the keeled slugs.

Resembling some toxic look-alikes despite being a well-regarded edible, this basidiomycete fungus is a fairly common species on well-drained soils across temperate Eurasia, found solitary or in fairy rings in pastures — name the species?
Macrolepiota procera is a basidiomycete fungus with a large, prominent fruiting body resembling a parasol.
This small southern-African mongoose has digging foreclaws and a knack for thermoregulating in harsh, dry country, living in tight packs of up to 30 — which sharp-eyed animal is it?
Meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.
Some of these tiny eight-legged arachnids live in soil as decomposers, others on plants causing galls, and one destructive parasite targets honeybee colonies — what are they?
Mite are small arachnids (eight-legged arthropods) of two large orders, the Acariformes and the Parasitiformes, which were historically grouped together in the subclass Acari.
This leafy Brassica rapa crop, native to the area around Beijing, became a widespread vegetable across Europe, the Americas, and Australia in the 1900s — which vegetable?
Napa cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp. In much of the world, it is referred to as "Chinese cabbage".
This basic mathematical object is used to count, measure, and label, most commonly represented today through the Hindu-Arabic system of ten symbols — what fundamental concept is it?
Number is a mathematical object used to count, measure, and label. The most basic examples are the natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so forth.
This Austrian striker had a brief, injury-hit loan spell at Inter Milan before becoming a regular at Werder Bremen and later playing for a Serbian club. Who is he?
Pan (genus) consists of two extant species: the bonobo and the chimpanzee.
Sprayed on clothing and mosquito nets or applied as a cream against lice and scabies, this pyrethroid discovered in 1972 is highly toxic to fish and to cats — what is it?
Permethrin is a medication and an insecticide.
A large, rounded body that orbits a star but isn't one itself — by the strictest definition, the Solar System has eight of these — what are they called?
Planet is a large, rounded astronomical body that is generally required to be in orbit around a star, stellar remnant, or brown dwarf, and is not one itself.

Caused by a mutation in a single gene that holds the cell nucleus together, this rare disorder makes children age much faster than normal, with most patients living only into their teens or twenties — what's the condition?
Progeria (also Hutchinson-Gilford syndrome or Hutchinson-Gilford progeroid syndrome; HGPS) is a type of progeroid syndrome.

This genus of roughly 1,750 flowering plant species, found worldwide mostly in temperate and mountainous regions, includes a tenacious creeping species common in European gardens as well as bulbous and meadow-dwelling relatives. What are these plants commonly called?
Ranunculus is a large genus of about 1750 species of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Native to West Africa and later naturalized across Asia and the West Indies, this plant's stems yield fibre while its calyces are steeped for a popular infusion — what is it?
Roselle (plant) (Sabdariffa gossypiifolia) is a species of flowering plant in the genus Sabdariffa that is native to Africa, most likely West Africa.
This synthetic element, atomic number 106, is so fleeting that only a few atoms exist at a time and decay within minutes — and it's named for an American nuclear chemist; what is it?
Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Commonly but inaccurately nicknamed for a big cat it wasn't closely related to, this extinct genus of saber-toothed predator roamed the Americas until as recently as 8,200 years ago — which genus?
Smilodon is a genus of extinct felids. It is one of the best-known saber-toothed predators and prehistoric mammals.
Co-founder of Apple Computer Company in 1976, he also purchased Pixar and returned as CEO in 1997. Who?
Steve Jobs (February 24, 1955 - October 5, 2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor.
Modern practitioners prioritize common ancestry as they sort living things into ranked taxa, from domain and kingdom all the way down to species — which biological discipline does this?

Taxonomy (biology) (from Ancient Greek (taxis) 'arrangement' and - (-nomia) 'method') is the scientific study of naming, defining (circumscribing) and classifying groups of biological organisms based on shared characteristics.
Joining Bethesda Game Studios in 1994, this video game director has since led development of both The Elder Scrolls and Fallout series, as well as 2023's Starfield. Who is he?
Todd Howard (born 1970) is an American video game designer, director, and producer who serves as director and executive producer at Bethesda Game Studios.

An oily, amber-colored liquid that's extremely non-volatile and therefore lingers in the environment, this organophosphorus compound was developed for chemical warfare and is lethal in doses of just tens of milligrams — which chemical agent?
VX (nerve agent) is an extremely toxic synthetic chemical compound in the organophosphorus class, specifically, a thiophosphonate.
Native to Eastern and Southern Africa, this large antelope genus includes two species — one black, one blue — whose lineages diverged roughly a million years ago — what animal is it?
Wildebeest (VIL-), also called gnu (NOO or, NEW), are antelopes of the genus Connochaetes and native to Eastern and Southern Africa.

These ear-shaped sea snails wear a shell with a row of breathing holes and a pearly inside, and their flesh is prized as a delicacy worldwide — about 70 species, the biggest a foot long. What are they?
Abalone: Common name for a group of sea snails.
One of the world's few semiaquatic vipers, this venomous pit viper of the southeastern United States coils and displays its fangs when threatened — what is it?
This genus of over 650 succulent species includes a 'true' member long used in pharmaceutical products, native to Africa, Madagascar, and the Arabian Peninsula — which genus?
Aloe: Genus of succulent flowering plants.
Despite helping develop the Soviet Union's thermonuclear weapons, this physicist won the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize for his human-rights activism and was later persecuted as a dissident — who was he?
Andrei Sakharov: Soviet nuclear physicist and human rights activist (1921–1989)
First described by Linnaeus in 1753, this Old World vegetable — better known on dinner plates as celery — is also cultivated for a bulbous root form called celeriac. What is its scientific name?
This common eye condition occurs when the cornea or lens is slightly egg-shaped rather than spherical, causing blurred vision at every distance?
This Caltech experimental physicist shared the 2017 Nobel with Rainer Weiss and Kip Thorne for the LIGO detector and the observation of gravitational waves — who is he?
Barry Barish: American physicist and Nobel Laureate (born 1936)
This interdisciplinary field examines moral questions raised by advances in biology, medicine, and biotechnology, touching everything from patient care to environmental policy — what is it called?
Bioethics: Study of the ethical issues emerging from advances in biology and medicine.
Built as a militarized derivative of a popular 737 airliner, this maritime patrol aircraft hunts submarines for the US Navy and allies like India, Australia and the UK — which aircraft?
Boeing P-8 Poseidon: American maritime patrol aircraft. The Boeing P-8 Poseidon is an American maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft developed and produced by Boeing Defense, Space & Security.

Characterized by cycles of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors like self-induced vomiting, this eating disorder has an estimated genetic risk factor between 30 and 80 percent — what is it called?
Bulimia nervosa: Eating disorder. Bulimia is more common among those who have a close relative with the condition.
Discovered in 1940 and making up as much as 40% of cannabis extract, this compound is an anticonvulsant used to treat two rare forms of childhood epilepsy — what is it?

Cannabidiol: Phytocannabinoid discovered in 1940. In the United States, the cannabidiol drug Epidiolex was approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2018, for the treatment of two seizure disorders.
Their young are calves and their castrated males are oxen; this widespread bovid is the most far-flung species of the genus Bos — what animal is it?
Traceable to fairy tales that weren't classified this way until the seventeenth century, this genre spans picture books for toddlers to young-adult fiction for teens — what category of writing?
Children's literature: Stories, books, magazines, and poems primarily written for children.
Sold under the brand name Klonopin, this long-acting benzodiazepine kicks in within an hour and lasts eight to twelve, treating anxiety, seizures, and panic — which drug is it?
Clonazepam: Benzodiazepine medication. It possesses anxiolytic, anticonvulsant, sedative, hypnotic, and skeletal muscle relaxant properties.

Nicknamed the deaf adder or long-cripple in parts of Europe, this legless, burrowing lizard has smooth scales that don't overlap — and despite its name, it's neither a snake nor what it sounds like. What is it?
Common slow worm: Species of legless lizard. The common slow worm (Anguis fragilis) is a non-venomous species of legless lizard native to Europe.
Stalked ones anchored to the seafloor are nicknamed 'sea lilies' while the free-swimming kind are 'feather stars' — what's the class name for these mouth-on-top echinoderms?
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded and serves as CEO of Roblox Corporation, after his earlier company was acquired by MSC Software in 1998 — who is he?

Cultivated in China for more than 2,000 years despite not being formally described until 1780, this tree produces the most widely grown fruit in its genus, known by names like Japanese or Chinese persimmon. Which species?
Diospyros kaki: Oriental fruit. Although its first botanical description was not published until 1780, D. kaki cultivation in China dates back more than 2000 years.
Known medically as cerumen, this waxy secretion in the ear canal protects against bacteria, fungi, and water while trapping dust and dead skin — what is it?
Earwax: Waxy substance secreted by the ear.
Continuous with the outer nuclear membrane and absent from red blood cells, this organelle comes in rough and smooth forms and handles protein folding — what is it?
Endoplasmic reticulum: Cell organelle that processes proteins.
Recognizable by its striking yellow-and-azure plumage, this small European songbird nests in tree holes and can acrobatically hang upside-down from branch tips — which bird?
Eurasian blue tit: Species of bird. The Eurasian blue tit (Cyanistes caeruleus) is a small passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae.
This German mathematician's 1872 Erlangen program reorganized all of geometry by its underlying symmetry groups, and he later turned Göttingen into a world center of research — who was he?
Home to the radius and ulna joined by the interosseous membrane, this region of the arm lies between the elbow and the wrist — what is it?
Forearm: Region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist.

In 1974 in Pacific Grove, California, this computer scientist demoed the first working prototype of CP/M and invented the BIOS, then founded Digital Research to sell his software — who was this PC-revolution pioneer?
Gary Kildall: American computer scientist and microcomputer entrepreneur (1942–1994)
Nicknamed creeping charlie and alehoof, this aromatic mint-family creeper is eaten as a salad green in some countries but reviled as an invasive lawn weed in North America — what plant is it?
Glechoma hederacea: Species of plant in the mint family. It is commonly known as ground-ivy, gill-over-the-ground, creeping charlie, alehoof, tunhoof, catsfoot, field balm, and run-away-robin.
Marketed under the brand name Mucinex, this expectorant medication has been used to loosen chest congestion since at least 1933 — what is it?
Guaifenesin: Expectorant medication. It may be used in combination with other medications.

Formally described only in 1983, this helical, flagella-driven bacterium burrows through the stomach's mucous lining and is the chief culprit behind gastric ulcers and some stomach cancers. What is it?
This extinct archaic human was the first to evolve a humanlike body and gait, the first to leave Africa for Asia and Europe, and the first to wield fire — who were they?
Homo erectus: Extinct species of archaic human. Homo erectus ( lit. 'upright man') is an extinct species of archaic human from the Pleistocene, spanning nearly 2 million years.

In this heart condition, the muscle walls, especially the wall between the ventricles, thicken without an obvious cause, weakening the heart's pumping and sometimes disrupting its electrical signals — which condition?

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: Enlargement of the heart muscle. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, or HOCM when obstructive) is a condition in which muscle tissues of the heart become thickened without an obvious cause.
Covering patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets, this legal category of intangible creations first developed as a concept in 17th- and 18th-century England — what is it called?
Intellectual property: Ownership of creative expressions and processes.
Caused by a buildup of bilirubin, this condition turns the skin and eyes yellowish and affects an estimated 80% of newborns in their first week of life — what is it?
Jaundice: Abnormal yellowish skin colour caused by high level of bilirubin.
This genus of coniferous trees and shrubs in the cypress family includes a species that forms the world's highest-known forest, at 4,900 metres in the Himalayas — what is it called?
This severe form of childhood protein malnutrition causes swelling and an enlarged, fatty liver, and is distinct from the calorie-deficient condition known as marasmus — what is it?
Kwashiorkor: Severe protein malnutrition. Kwashiorkor ( KWOSH-ee-OR-kor, -⁠kər) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.
Marked by weariness and a desire to act without the energy to do so, which condition can be a normal response to poor sleep or stress, or a sign of underlying illness?
Lethargy: State of tiredness, weariness, fatigue, or lack of energy.
Reaching about 200 kg at its largest, this reddish-brown-shelled reptile ranges through the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean — which species?
Loggerhead sea turtle: Species of marine reptile distributed throughout the world.
A former mayor of Tehran and engineer by training, he served as Iran's sixth president from 2005 to 2013 and championed the country's nuclear program — who is he?

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad: President of Iran from 2005 to 2013. Mahmoud Ahmadinejad (né Sabbaghian; born 28 October 1956) is an Iranian politician who served as the sixth president of Iran from 2005 to 2013.

Belonging to the ancient order Ephemeroptera and keeping primitive traits like long tails and wings that won't fold flat, which aquatic insect's water-dwelling nymphs signal a clean, unpolluted stream?
Mayfly: Aquatic insects of the order Ephemeroptera. Over 3,000 species of mayfly are known worldwide, grouped into over 400 genera in 42 families.
This colorless gas, made by swapping one hydrogen atom in ammonia for a methyl group, has a strong rotten-fish smell and serves as a building block for many compounds — what is it?
Native to Southeast Asia, this evergreen tree's leaves are known as kratom, containing alkaloids that bind to opioid receptors — which species?
Mitragyna speciosa: Species of plant. It is under preliminary research for possible antipsychotic and antidepressant properties.
Despite its name, this blister-agent chemical weapon isn't always gaseous, and to this day there is no antidote for exposure to it — what is it?
Mustard gas: Chemical warfare agent. There is no preventive agent against mustard gas, with protection depending entirely on skin and airways protection, and no antidote exists for mustard poisoning.
This medical specialty diagnoses and treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves, from epilepsy and stroke to Parkinson's disease — which field?
Neurology: Medical specialty dealing with disorders of the nervous system.
Grown worldwide as ornamentals in ponds and known to gardeners simply as water lilies, this widespread genus of aquatic plants also includes species considered weeds — which genus?
Nymphaea: Genus of aquatic plants. Nymphaea is a genus of hardy and tender aquatic plants in the family Nymphaeaceae.
This Romanian-American engineer served as Team Principal of the Alpine Formula One team from February 2022 to July 2023 — who is he?
Otmar Szafnauer: American-Romanian engineer, F1 team lead.
Found in mice, cats, birds, humans, and dogs but absent in whales and most reptiles, this triangular bone is the body's largest sesamoid — what is it?
Patella: Kneecap, bone covering knee joint.
What is this — “Abnormal growth of scar tissue within the penis”?

Peyronie's disease: Abnormal growth of scar tissue within the penis. The plaques cause abnormal curvature, pain, penile deformities (e.g., narrowing or indentation), and usually erectile dysfunction, particularly during erection.

A member of the cashew family, this tree nut is a priority allergen, yet the world still churned out 1.4 million tonnes in 2024 — with the US, Iran, and Turkey making up 87% of it. Which green-hued nut is it?
Pistachio: Member of the cashew family. The pistachio (UK also; Pistacia vera) is a small to medium-sized tree of the cashew family.
This imperial unit of pressure equals about 6.895 kilopascals and is the number you check when filling a bicycle tire to around 65 — which unit?
Pound per square inch: Unit of pressure or stress. It is the pressure resulting from a force with magnitude of one pound-force applied to an area of one square inch.

Described as 'the translation of politics into the reality that citizens experience every day,' this field implements government policies and programs to solve social and economic problems — what is it called?
